Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.question: When an invited email belongs to an existing member (possibly hidden), what does the inviter see?
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.answer: Always tell me exactly what happened — 'already a member, added to your roster' vs 'signup invite sent'
options_presented: Tell me only when they're publicly findable (recommended)
Always the same neutral message
Always tell me exactly what happened
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.note: Chosen with the tradeoff stated in the option text: this makes the invite box a way to test whether any address has a Funūn account, including deliberately hidden members. Accepted knowingly, and mitigated by the next decision rather than left open.

Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.question: What stops bulk enumeration now that the box confirms membership?
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.answer: Both — notify the person they were added/looked up, AND cap lookups per member per day
options_presented: Tell the person they were looked up (recommended)
Hard rate limit plus audit log
Both
Nothing for now — beta is small
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.note: The two cover different failure modes: the cap defeats volume, the notice defeats quiet targeted checks on one specific person. Exact cap value not yet set.

Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.question: What happens when the address belongs to someone who has blocked the inviter?
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.answer: The action ends — no email of any kind, no roster entry, no disclosure
options_presented: The action ends — nothing sent, nothing added (recommended)
Add to my private roster, but contact nobody
Treat them as a non-member and send the signup invite
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.note: This is what makes the full-disclosure choice defensible. A block must be unroutable; if any path still delivers a message or confirms the account, the block is decorative. discover_profile_id_by_email already enforces no_block both directions — the NEW reconciliation path is where that could have been routed around.

Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.question: What recourse does the notified person have?
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.answer: Informational notice with a block link; no separate removal mechanism
options_presented: Informational, with a block link (recommended)
They can request removal from that roster
Purely informational, no action in the email
Invisible reconciliation — what the invi.note: No new mechanism needed — the block remedy already exists and, per the previous decision, is now total. Being on a private list that grants nothing is not a harm needing its own dispute flow.

What 'Add to roster' creates for a found.question: What happens to PRO/IPI/publisher, which are private and excluded from the discovery projection?
What 'Add to roster' creates for a found.answer: OWNER MODEL, in the owner's words: rights data lives in the member's own settings; if present the system already knows and she does nothing; if missing, a contextual form field asks her AND updates her settings rather than making a copy; the system holds it but does NOT disclose it to the roster owner 'until it is needed on a contract or an upload for a distributor or something similar where it is required'
options_presented: Blank, marked awaiting-her (offered)
Let me type them, marked as my guess (offered)
Prompt her to share when notified (offered)
What 'Add to roster' creates for a found.note: The owner rejected all three offered options in favour of a deferred-disclosure model. The real promise is 'don't make me re-enter things', NOT 'show me my collaborator's identifiers'. Three disclosure triggers named and left undecided: document need, explicit grant (artist lets a supervisor see it), and project-membership blanket access for release. Existing machinery for the third: project_members (078), work_members + work_member_tier (136).
